paite: Huchi a Judah leh Benjamin melmate'n saltangte tate'n TOUPA, Israel' Pathian a ding in tempul alam uh chih azak un;
heading: Tempul Lam Thak Ding Dalna
english: Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to Yahweh, the God of Israel,

paite: Zerubbabel leh pipute inko lupente kiang ah ahong pai nai ua, akiang uah, "Hon lampih le ung ake: noute bang in, na Pathian uh lah ka zong ngal ua; Assuria kumpipa Esarhaddon in hiai mun ahon pipa dam lai nite a kipan amah kiang ah ka kithoih uhi," achi uhi.
english: they came near to Zerubbabel, and to the heads of fathers’ households, and said to them, “Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do; and we have been sacrificing to him since the days of Esar Haddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”

paite: Himahleh Zerubbabel leh Jeshua leh Israel pipu inko lupente'n akiang uah, "Ka Pathian uh a dia inn na hon lampihna ding ziak bangmah na nei kei uh; himahleh Persia kumpipa Kura in kou thu ahon piak bang in, Israel' Pathian, TOUPA a ding in koute'n ka lam ding uhi," achi uhi.
english: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of fathers’ households of Israel said to them, “You have nothing to do with us in building a house to our God; but we ourselves together will build to Yahweh, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.”

paite: Huchi in gam a mite'n Judah a mite khut ahatsakta kei ua, inn lamna ah amau asubuaita uhi.
english: Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building.

paite: Persia kumpipa Kura dam lai tengteng, Persia kumpipa Darias lal lai tanpha in, athiltup uh kalhse ding, amaute siatna ding in thuhilh mite aguai uhi.
english: They hired counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.

paite: Ahasueras vaihawm pat tung lai in, Judah leh Jerusalem a tengte hekna lai agelh uhi.
heading: Jerusalem Lam Thak Ding Dalna
english: In the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

paite: Huan Artaksarses dam lai in Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel leh akithuahpihte'n Persia kumpipa Artaksarses kiang ah lai agelh ua; laikhak gelhdan Siria laimal a gelh a, Siria pau a bawlkhiak ahi.
english: In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his companions wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the writing of the letter was written in Syrian and delivered in the Syrian language.

paite: Sepaih heutu lian Rehum leh laigelhmi Shimshai in Jerusalem siatna ding in kumpipa Artaksarses kiang ah hichibang in laikhak agelh uhi.
english: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows.

paite: Sepaih heutu lian Rehum leh laigelhmi Shimshai leh akithuahpihte un huchi in agelhta ua; Dinai mite, Apharsatki mite, Tarpe mite, Aphar mite, Arki mite, Babulon mite, Susan mite, Deha mite, Elam mite leh,
english: Then Rehum the chancellor, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their companions, the Dinaites, and the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Shushanchites, the Dehaites, the Elamites,

paite: Osnappar lian leh thupi in apikhiak, Samaria khopi leh luipi khen a gamdang leh adangdang a kikoih namte tan in.
english: and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Osnappar brought over and settled in the city of Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River, and so forth, wrote.

paite: Kumpipa Artaksarses kiang a alaikhak uh teisawn hiai ahi: "Luipi khen lam leh adangdang a na sikhate.
english: This is the copy of the letter that they sent: To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the people beyond the River.

paite: Na kiang a kipan a hong tou Judate Jerusalem ah kou kiang ah ahong uh chih kumpipa kiang ah theih in om hen: Khopi helhat leh hoih lou alam lellel ua, akulhbaangte azouta ua, asuangphumte apuah khinta uh.
english: Be it known to the king that the Jews who came up from you have come to us to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and bad city, and have finished the walls and repaired the foundations.

paite: Kumpipa'n thei hen, hiai khopi lam a a-om a, akulhbaangte zoh in omleh zaw, leimante, siahte sumsinna leimante hiam lamlian leimante ape kei ding ua, atawptawp in kumpipa siatna ahi ding.
english: Be it known now to the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it will be hurtful to the kings.

paite: Tu in koute kumpi inn a pan huhna ngahte ka hih ziak un, kumpipa zahlakna muh koute ding in akilawm kei a, huaiziak in kumpipa thudik ka hon khak uhi.
english: Now because we eat the salt of the palace and it is not appropriate for us to see the king’s dishonor, therefore we have sent and informed the king,

paite: Na pipute chiamtehna laibu sung ah kizong hen: huchi in chiamtehna laibu sung ah na mu ding a, hiai khopi helhat, kumpipate leh bialte a dia poikhoih hat chih leh nidanglai mah in leng huai sung mah a helna ana bawlta uh chih na thei mai ding; huaiziak a hiai khopi kihihsegawp lah ahi ngal a.
english: that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will see in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful to kings and provinces, and that they have started rebellions within it in the past. That is why this city was destroyed.

paite: Hiai khopi akilam a, akulhbaangte hichibang a akihih khitleh zaw, luipi khen lam ah tan na nei kei ding chih kumpipa ka hon theitelsak uhi," chi in.
english: We inform the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, then you will have no possession beyond the River.

paite: Huchi in dansiam Rehum leh laigelhmi Shimshai leh Samaria leh luipi khen a gam a teng akithuahpih tengteng kiang ah kumpipa'n dawnna akhak hi: Chibai,
english: Then the king sent an answer to Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companions who live in Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River: Peace.

paite: "Laikhak ka kiang a na hon khak uh ka ma ah teltak a sim ahita.
english: The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me.

paite: Huchi in thu ka pia a, akizong khin a, nidanglai in hiai khopi in kumpipate tung ah helna abawl a, huai ah helpina leh helna a na kibawlta chih muhkhiak in a-om hi.
english: I decreed, and search has been made, and it was found that this city has made insurrection against kings in the past, and that rebellion and revolts have been made in it.

paite: Huai lou in kumpipa thilhihthei taktak, luipi khen gam tengteng tung a vaihawm, Jerusalem tung a vaihawmte ana om ua; van leimante, sumsinna leimante leh lamlian leimante amau kiang a piak ahi hi.
english: There have also been mighty kings over Jerusalem who have ruled over all the country beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll was paid to them.

paite: Huchi in keimah in thupiak ka bawl masiah, huai mite khawl ding leh hiai khopi lam lou ding in, thupiak bawl un.
english: Make a decree now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built until a decree is made by me.

paite: Hiai thu a ze-ol lou ding in pilvang un: Bang ding in kumpipate siatna ding in hoihlouhna akhang dia?" chi in.
english: Be careful that you not be slack doing so. Why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?

paite: Huchi a kumpipa Artaksarses laikhak teisawn Rehum leh laigelhmi Shimshai leh akithuahpihte ma a asim khit un, kintak in Jerusalem a Judate kiang ah ahoh ua, kihatsakna leh thilhihtheihna zang in amau akhawlsakta uhi.
english: Then when the copy of King Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and made them to cease by force of arms.

paite: Huchi in Jerusalem a Pathian inn nasep akhawl a: Persia kumpipa Darias vaihawm akum nihna tan in akhawl hi.
english: Then work stopped on God’s house which is at Jerusalem. It stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
